text:
The goaltending question in New Jersey was supposed to be settled when the Devils traded for Connor Hellebuyck in October. On Saturday in St. Louis, he was pulled after a disastrous first period of what became a 9-6 loss, and the week's headlines about him went beyond hockey: Hellebuyck has said the threats against his family went beyond online death threats, per Yahoo Sports.

The skaters have held up their end. New Jersey has 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 57% at 5-on-5 too, and it draws more penalties than it takes. Both top lines win about 60% of the chances: Timo Meier, Nico Hischier and Luke Evangelista, and Jesper Bratt, Jack Hughes and Arseny Gritsyuk, who have outscored teams 12-8. Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes have been on for 22 goals for and 12 against at 5-on-5. Meier stayed hot with a goal in Monday's 3-2 win over Columbus, which snapped a two-game skid.

What hasn't held is the net. The Devils have allowed about 9.6 more goals than their chances against predict, and Jake Allen's last five starts came at .858, 4.5 goals worse than expected.

At 16-8-0, our playoff odds have them at 95%. Anton Silaev was sent back to Utica this week. What we'd watch: whether Hellebuyck puts Saturday behind him, because the skaters are doing their job.
headline: The Devils win the chances and still search in net
